mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR (to derive its conversion ratio) alongside Team B's shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST (to derive its defensive filtering ratio). The mechanism fires when one side has high shot volume but low on-target ratio while the opponent suppresses shots allowed to a low absolute level.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's shots-to-on-target ratio is low and Team B's shots-allowed level is well below competition average, Team A's on-target output is suppressed below what its raw shot volume alone would predict — i.e. the two ratios interact multiplicatively rather than additively.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume is high but its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target / shots) is low relative to Team B's, while Team B concedes very few shots against. The joint relationship between Team A's shot-to-on-target ratio and Team B's shots-allowed suppression determines whether Team A's volume translates into meaningful on-target threat, or is neutralised by Team B's defensive structure.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both sides simultaneously — a four-variable joint relationship. It cannot be reduced to a single observable compared against one opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's possession FOR and Team A's shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST. Measure whether matches where Team B holds possession above a threshold co-occur with Team A facing shots-against volumes that exceed what Team A's defensive shots-allowed average alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's shots-against volume rises with Team B's possession share in a non-linear fashion — the relationship steepens once possession crosses a saturation threshold rather than scaling linearly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B dominates possession (>60%) while Team A concedes high possession and faces high shots against. The joint relationship between Team B's possession share and Team A's shots-against volume tests whether possession dominance by Team B translates into a disproportionate shots-against burden for Team A beyond what each observable predicts independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable relationship (possession and shots/shots_on_target) across asymmetric sides, with a threshold/saturation test on a continuous possession variable. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's fouls FOR (committed) and Team B's corner_kicks FOR. In matches where Team A's foul rate is elevated above its own season average, measure whether Team B's corner count also rises above Team B's baseline corner production — testing a cross-observable interaction between one team's disciplinary output and the opponent's set-piece volume.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner-kick volume rises with Team A's foul rate — the relationship is positive and potentially non-linear, with corner counts increasing more steeply once Team A's fouls exceed a threshold above the competition mean.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits fouls at a high rate (especially in recent matches) while Team B earns corners at a moderate rate. The joint relationship between Team A's foul rate and Team B's corner-kick production tests whether Team A's foul-heavy style inflates Team B's set-piece opportunities (corners) beyond what Team B's corner production average alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team, cross-observable relationship (Team A fouls → Team B corners). It cannot be reduced to either observable alone against a single opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's yellow_cards FOR trend (recent vs. all-prior) and Team B's cards_2h FOR (second-half cards earned). Measure whether the co-occurrence of Team A's elevated recent yellow-card rate and Team B's above-average second-half card rate produces a second-half total-cards environment above competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume is elevated when Team A's yellow-card rate is trending upward (recent > season average) and Team B's cards_2h rate is simultaneously above competition average — the joint condition produces a super-additive disciplinary environment in the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's yellow card rate has risen sharply in recent matches relative to its season average, while Team B earns a high cards_2h rate in the second half. The joint relationship between Team A's escalating yellow-card trend and Team B's second-half card-earning pattern tests whether the combination of a foul-prone Team A and a card-drawing Team B produces a second-half disciplinary environment that exceeds what either team's card rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly relating three observables (yellow_cards, cards_2h, fouls) across both teams with a within-match period split (second half) and a trend dimension (recent vs. all-prior). It is not reducible to any single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's goals FOR split by half (first-half vs. second-half) and Team A's goals AGAINST split by half. Measure whether the combination of Team B's first-half scoring tendency and Team A's first-half defensive vulnerability produces a first-half goals environment that exceeds the competition's half-level baseline more than either team's individual half-split would suggest.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: First-half goal volume is elevated when Team B's first-half scoring rate is above its own second-half rate and Team A's first-half goals-against rate is simultaneously above its own second-half goals-against rate — the joint half-level asymmetry across both teams concentrates goals in the first half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B scores a disproportionate share of its goals in the first half relative to the second half, while Team A concedes more in the first half than the second half. The joint first-half vs. second-half goal-timing asymmetry across both teams — where Team B's first-half goal rate is high and Team A's first-half goals-against rate is also high — tests whether the two teams' half-level goal distributions interact to concentrate match goals in the first half beyond what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split applied jointly across two distinct team perspectives (Team B attacking, Team A defending), comparing the two halves simultaneously for both sides. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band or a simple home/away split.
